groups.subject: chemistry
groups.title: Amines
groups.passage_text:
In a laboratory preparation, 9.3 g of aniline (0.10 mol) is dissolved in an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid, and the flask is kept in an ice-salt bath so that the temperature stays between 273 K and 278 K. A cold solution containing exactly the stoichiometric amount of sodium nitrite is added slowly with stirring. The clear solution obtained is never allowed to warm up and is used at once, without isolating any solid from it. It is then divided into four equal portions, labelled P, Q, R and S.

Portion P is poured into a cold alkaline solution of phenol, and an orange-red solid separates at once. Portion Q is treated with aqueous potassium iodide at room temperature; bubbles of a colourless gas escape and a dense, dark oil settles at the bottom. Portion R is added to a warm solution of cuprous cyanide and potassium cyanide; the same colourless gas is evolved, and a colourless liquid with a bitter-almond smell distils over. Portion S is simply left on the bench in a warm room for an hour; it also evolves the colourless gas, and its smell changes to that of a phenolic disinfectant.

Every reaction in this preparation goes to completion, and the organic products from P, Q and R all retain the benzene ring of the original aniline.

groups.subject: gat
groups.title: Numerical Ability
groups.passage_text: Meera runs a stationery shop. At the start of a month she borrowed Rs 20,000 at 12 per cent simple interest per annum for 6 months and spent the entire amount on 400 identical notebooks. She marked each notebook at 40 per cent above its cost price. During the month she sold 200 notebooks at a discount of 10 per cent on the marked price and the remaining 200 notebooks at the marked price. In the following month she bought the same notebooks again at the same cost, raised the marked price by 10 per cent over the earlier marked price, and then announced a festival discount of 10 per cent on the new marked price.

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following stages in the development of a dicot embryo in the order in which they appear after fertilisation.
(A) Heart-shaped embryo
(B) Mature embryo
(C) Zygote
(D) Globular embryo
rows.explanation: The zygote divides to form a proembryo, which becomes a rounded globular mass of cells, then a heart-shaped embryo as the two cotyledons begin to form, and finally the mature embryo. The heart-shaped stage cannot come before the globular stage, because the cotyledon primordia arise only from the rounded cell mass. Placing the mature embryo before the heart-shaped stage ignores the order of cotyledon growth.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants: post-fertilisation events, embryo development in dicots (zygote, proembryo, globular, heart-shaped, mature embryo)

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: In a typical angiosperm fruit, which two parts develop from tissues of the mother plant and not from the products of fertilisation?
rows.explanation: The seed coat develops from the integuments and the pericarp from the ovary wall, and both are tissues of the mother plant. The embryo arises from the zygote and the endosperm from the primary endosperm cell, so both are products of fertilisation. Pairing the embryo with the seed coat is a common slip because both lie inside the seed.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants: post-fertilisation events, seed and fruit formation (integuments to seed coat, ovary wall to pericarp)

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: In a human female, the secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division:

options.text: Only when a sperm enters its cytoplasm
Shortly before ovulation, inside the Graafian follicle
At puberty, when the menstrual cycles begin
During foetal life, before the female is born

rows.explanation: The secondary oocyte released at ovulation is arrested at metaphase II. Only when a sperm enters does it complete the second meiotic division, forming a haploid ovum and a second polar body. Completing meiosis I shortly before ovulation inside the Graafian follicle is a different step, which produces the secondary oocyte and the first polar body.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Human Reproduction: oogenesis and fertilisation, completion of the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: At implantation in humans, which part of the blastocyst becomes attached to the endometrium, and which part gives rise to the embryo?

options.text: Inner cell mass attaches; trophoblast forms the embryo
Trophoblast attaches; trophoblast forms the embryo
Trophoblast attaches; inner cell mass forms the embryo
Trophoblast attaches; inner cell mass forms the placenta

rows.explanation: The blastocyst has an outer trophoblast layer and an inner cell mass. The trophoblast cells contact and attach to the endometrium during implantation, while the inner cell mass differentiates into the embryo. The placenta is formed by trophoblast-derived tissue together with maternal tissue, so assigning it to the inner cell mass reverses the roles.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Human Reproduction: cleavage, blastocyst (trophoblast and inner cell mass) and implantation

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Amniocentesis (B) MTP (C) IUI (D) ZIFT
List-II: (I) Transfer of a zygote or early embryo of up to eight blastomeres into the fallopian tube (II) Intentional termination of pregnancy before full term (III) Artificial introduction of semen into the vagina or uterus (IV) Analysis of foetal cells in the amniotic fluid for chromosomal abnormalities
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: Amniocentesis tests foetal cells shed into the amniotic fluid for chromosomal abnormalities, and MTP is the intentional termination of pregnancy before full term. IUI places semen artificially into the vagina or uterus, whereas ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo of up to eight blastomeres into the fallopian tube. Swapping IUI and ZIFT is the usual slip, since both are assisted reproduction methods.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Reproductive Health: amniocentesis, MTP, assisted reproductive technologies (IUI, ZIFT)

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Consider the following statements about two genetic disorders of humans.
(A) In sickle-cell anaemia, valine is replaced by glutamic acid at the sixth position of the beta globin chain.
(B) Thalassemia results from a reduced rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains.
(C) A person with the genotype HbAHbS is a carrier who is apparently unaffected.
(D) Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: In sickle-cell anaemia the sixth amino acid of the beta globin chain changes from glutamic acid to valine, so the substitution is stated backwards in the first statement. Thalassemia is a quantitative defect with too little globin made, the HbAHbS genotype is an apparently unaffected carrier, and sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Principles of Inheritance and Variation: Mendelian disorders, sickle-cell anaemia and thalassemia

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: A queen honey bee has 32 chromosomes in her body cells. A drone that develops from one of her unfertilised eggs will have how many chromosomes in its body cells and in each of its sperms?
rows.explanation: An unfertilised honey bee egg is haploid, so the drone has 16 chromosomes in its body cells, half of 32. A haploid cell has no homologous pairs to separate, so the drone makes sperms by mitosis and each sperm keeps 16 chromosomes. Answering 16 and 8 wrongly assumes that meiosis halves the number again.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Principles of Inheritance and Variation: sex determination in honey bee (haplodiploidy)

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following events of protein synthesis in a cell in the order in which they occur.
(A) Elongation of the polypeptide by the sequential addition of amino acids
(B) Charging of tRNA with its amino acid
(C) Binding of a release factor to the stop codon
(D) Binding of the ribosome to mRNA at the start codon
rows.explanation: The tRNAs are first charged with their specific amino acids, then the ribosome binds mRNA at the start codon AUG, which only the initiator tRNA recognises. The polypeptide then lengthens codon by codon during elongation, and a release factor binding the stop codon ends translation. Elongation cannot precede initiation, because there is no chain to extend until the ribosome is assembled at the start codon.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Molecular Basis of Inheritance: translation, charging of tRNA, initiation, elongation and termination

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: In the Hershey-Chase experiment, bacteria infected with bacteriophages labelled with radioactive sulphur (35S) were blended and then centrifuged. Where was most of the radioactivity found?

options.text: In the pellet, as viral DNA that entered the bacteria
In the pellet, as viral protein that had entered the bacteria
In the supernatant, as viral DNA that stayed outside the bacteria
In the supernatant, as viral protein left outside the bacteria

rows.explanation: Sulphur occurs in the amino acids of proteins but not in DNA, so 35S labels the phage protein coat. Blending shakes the empty coats off the bacterial surface and they stay in the supernatant after centrifugation, while the bacteria settle in the pellet. It was the 32P-labelled DNA that was found inside the infected bacteria, which showed that DNA is the genetic material.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Molecular Basis of Inheritance: search for genetic material, Hershey-Chase experiment

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: The template strand of a gene segment reads 3'-TACGGATCC-5'. The anticodon, written 3' to 5', of the tRNA that pairs with the third codon of the mRNA transcribed from it is:
rows.explanation: Transcription of the template strand 3'-TACGGATCC-5' gives the mRNA 5'-AUGCCUAGG-3', whose third codon is AGG. The anticodon pairs with its codon in an antiparallel manner, so it is 3'-UCC-5', the template triplet with U in place of T. Writing the codon itself as the anticodon is one slip, and 3'-GGA-5' is the anticodon of the second codon.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Molecular Basis of Inheritance: genetic code, tRNA anticodon and translation

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: An electric discharge was passed through a closed flask containing a mixture of gases in Miller's experiment. Which gas was absent from that mixture?
rows.explanation: Miller passed an electric discharge through a closed flask containing methane, hydrogen, ammonia and water vapour at about 800 °C, imitating the primitive reducing atmosphere, and obtained amino acids. Free oxygen was left out because the early atmosphere had none. Methane, ammonia and hydrogen were all part of the mixture.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Evolution: origin of life, Miller's experiment

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: In a population of seed-eating birds, birds with very small or very large beaks feed efficiently, while birds with medium-sized beaks feed poorly. Which change in the beak-size distribution is expected over many generations?

options.text: Two peaks, with intermediate beaks becoming rare
One narrower peak around the mean beak size
One peak shifted towards larger beaks
One peak shifted towards smaller beaks

rows.explanation: When both extremes of a trait are favoured and the average is disadvantaged, the distribution splits into two peaks and the intermediate type becomes rare; this is disruptive selection. A single narrower peak at the mean is the outcome of stabilising selection, and a peak shifted to one side is directional selection, which does not fit a situation in which both extremes do well.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Evolution: mechanism of evolution, natural selection and its types

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: A patient has sustained high fever of 39 to 40 degrees Celsius, weakness, stomach pain, constipation and headache, and typhoid is suspected. Which test is used to confirm the diagnosis?
rows.explanation: Typhoid, caused by Salmonella typhi, is confirmed by the Widal test, which detects the patient's antibodies against the bacterium. ELISA is the test used to detect HIV infection and is the nearest wrong choice, but it is not the confirmatory test for typhoid. Biopsy is used to examine tissue for cancer, and PCR for early detection of HIV or of cancer genes.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 Human Health and Disease: typhoid, its symptoms and confirmation by the Widal test

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: On exposure to pollen, a person develops sneezing and watery eyes. Which pair correctly names the type of antibody involved and the cells that release histamine?
rows.explanation: In allergy the immune system overreacts to an allergen such as pollen and makes IgE antibodies, which trigger mast cells to release histamine and serotonin; these cause sneezing and watery eyes. IgA is the antibody found in colostrum, and macrophages are phagocytes, so neither is the source of histamine in an allergic response.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 Human Health and Disease: allergy, IgE antibodies and release of histamine from mast cells

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following events of HIV replication in a human host in the correct sequence.
(A) Progeny viruses released into the blood attack other helper T lymphocytes
(B) Viral RNA is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase
(C) Viral DNA is incorporated into the DNA of the infected cell
(D) HIV enters a macrophage
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: After HIV enters a macrophage, its RNA genome is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase, and this viral DNA is incorporated into the host cell's DNA, which then directs the production of new viruses. The progeny viruses released into the blood go on to attack helper T lymphocytes. Integration cannot come before reverse transcription, because the viral genome stays RNA until it has been copied.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 Human Health and Disease: AIDS, replication of HIV in macrophages and helper T lymphocytes

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: A drug obtained by acetylation of morphine is taken by snorting or injection. Which option correctly gives the drug, its source plant and its effect on body functions?

options.text: Cocaine; Erythroxylum coca; stimulates the central nervous system
Heroin; Papaver somniferum; slows down body functions
Heroin; Cannabis sativa; slows down body functions
Heroin; Papaver somniferum; stimulates the central nervous system

rows.explanation: Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is made by acetylating morphine, which is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant Papaver somniferum, and it is a depressant that slows down body functions. Cocaine from Erythroxylum coca is the stimulant, and Cannabis sativa gives marijuana and hashish, so those rows describe other drugs.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 Human Health and Disease: drugs and alcohol abuse, opioids, cannabinoids and coca alkaloids

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following events in the conversion of milk into curd in the correct sequence.
(A) Coagulation and partial digestion of milk proteins by the acid
(B) Addition of a small amount of curd to fresh milk
(C) Multiplication of lactic acid bacteria at a suitable temperature
(D) Production of lactic acid from the sugar of the milk
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: The curd added to fresh milk supplies lactic acid bacteria as a starter. At a suitable temperature they multiply and make lactic acid from the milk sugar, and this acid then coagulates and partially digests the milk proteins to give curd. The acid cannot be formed before the bacteria have been added and have multiplied, so the protein change comes last.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare: microbes in household products, conversion of milk to curd by lactic acid bacteria

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following events of the secondary treatment of sewage in the correct sequence.
(A) Aerobic microbes grow into flocs while the BOD of the effluent falls
(B) Effluent from the primary settling tank is aerated in a large tank
(C) The remaining sludge is digested by anaerobic bacteria in digesters
(D) Flocs settle in a settling tank to form activated sludge
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: In secondary treatment the primary effluent is aerated, aerobic microbes grow into flocs and lower the BOD, the flocs settle as activated sludge, and the part of the sludge not returned to the aeration tank goes to anaerobic digesters. Settling cannot come before floc formation, and sludge can be digested only after it has been collected.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare: secondary treatment of sewage, activated sludge and anaerobic sludge digesters

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Microbe): (A) Aspergillus niger (B) Acetobacter aceti (C) Saccharomyces cerevisiae (D) Streptococcus
List-II (Product): (I) Streptokinase (II) Ethanol (III) Citric acid (IV) Acetic acid
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: Aspergillus niger, a fungus, yields citric acid; Acetobacter aceti, a bacterium, yields acetic acid; the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae yields ethanol; and Streptococcus produces streptokinase, used as a clot buster. The nearest wrong mapping swaps the yeast and the bacterium, giving ethanol to Streptococcus and streptokinase to the yeast.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare: microbes in industrial products, organic acids, ethanol and streptokinase

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Which of the following statements about microbial products are correct?
(A) Wine and beer are produced without distillation of the fermented broth.
(B) Whisky, brandy and rum are produced without distillation of the fermented broth.
(C) Lipases are used as clot busters in patients who have had a myocardial infarction.
(D) Penicillin was named after the mould Penicillium notatum.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: Wine and beer are obtained by yeast fermentation without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy and rum need distillation of the fermented broth. The clot buster is streptokinase, while lipases are added to detergents to remove oily stains. Penicillin took its name from the mould Penicillium notatum, so only the first and last statements are correct.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare: fermented beverages, antibiotics and enzymes in industrial products

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: Statins are bioactive molecules obtained from the yeast Monascus purpureus. Their medical use depends on their ability to:

options.text: Dissolve blood clots that have blocked the arteries supplying the heart muscle
Suppress the immune response that causes rejection of a transplanted organ
Lower blood cholesterol by competitively inhibiting the enzyme that synthesises it
Kill disease-causing bacteria that have entered the tissues of the body

rows.explanation: Statins are competitive inhibitors of the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol, so they lower blood cholesterol. Dissolving clots is the role of streptokinase, immune suppression after transplants is the role of cyclosporin A, and killing bacteria is the role of antibiotics such as penicillin.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare: bioactive molecules, statins from Monascus purpureus

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: A farmer wants to protect crop roots from fungal pathogens without using chemical fungicides. Which of the following biocontrol agents should the farmer use?
rows.explanation: Trichoderma is a free-living fungus common in root ecosystems and is an effective biocontrol agent against several plant pathogens. Bacillus thuringiensis and baculoviruses are used against insect pests such as caterpillars, and the ladybird beetle feeds on aphids, so none of them acts against fungal pathogens.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare: microbes as biocontrol agents, Trichoderma against plant pathogens

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following steps of the polymerase chain reaction in the correct sequence.
(A) Extension of the primers by Taq polymerase
(B) Annealing of primers to the template strands
(C) Mixing the template DNA, primers, Taq polymerase and nucleotides in a tube
(D) Denaturation of the template DNA by heating
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: A PCR starts with the template, primers, thermostable Taq polymerase and nucleotides in one tube. Heating denatures the double-stranded template, cooling lets the primers anneal to the separated strands, and Taq polymerase then extends the primers. Annealing cannot come before denaturation, because primers can bind only to single strands.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes: polymerase chain reaction, denaturation, annealing and extension

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: Which sequence of a cloning vector is responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked foreign DNA?
rows.explanation: The origin of replication is the sequence from which replication starts, and any DNA linked to it is replicated in the host; it also controls the copy number of the linked DNA. A selectable marker only helps to identify transformants, and a recognition site is only where the vector is cut.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes: features of a cloning vector, origin of replication

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: In a stirred-tank bioreactor, the stirrer is mainly used to:

options.text: Rupture the host cells and release the product into the medium
Mix the contents evenly and ensure oxygen availability throughout
Sterilise the culture medium before the host cells are added
Separate and purify the product from the culture broth

rows.explanation: The stirrer of a stirred-tank bioreactor mixes the contents evenly and makes oxygen available throughout the vessel, so that the host cells grow under optimum conditions. Separation and purification of the product belong to downstream processing, and the medium is sterilised separately before inoculation.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes: bioreactors, stirred-tank type

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: A student isolating DNA from plant leaves wants to break the cell wall and then free the DNA of RNA and proteins. Which combination of enzymes should be used?

options.text: Cellulase for the cell wall, ribonuclease for RNA and protease for proteins
Lysozyme for the cell wall, ribonuclease for RNA and protease for proteins
Chitinase for the cell wall, ribonuclease for RNA and protease for proteins
Cellulase for the cell wall, ribonuclease for proteins and protease for RNA

rows.explanation: Plant cell walls are digested by cellulase, RNA is removed by ribonuclease and proteins by protease. Lysozyme is used for bacterial cells and chitinase for fungal cells, so they suit other sources, and the last combination assigns ribonuclease and protease to the wrong substrates.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes: isolation of genetic material, enzymes used to lyse cells and remove RNA and proteins

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following steps in the development of an insect-resistant transgenic plant in the correct order.
(A) Regeneration of whole plants from the transformed cells by tissue culture
(B) Insertion of the cry gene into the Ti plasmid
(C) Isolation of the cry gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
(D) Infection of plant explants with Agrobacterium carrying the recombinant plasmid
rows.explanation: The foreign gene must first be isolated, then placed in a vector such as the Ti plasmid, then delivered into plant cells by Agrobacterium, and only then can whole plants be regenerated from the transformed cells by tissue culture. Infecting explants before the gene is cloned into the plasmid would deliver nothing, since the bacterium can carry only what has already been inserted.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications: Bt crops and the steps in making a transgenic plant (Ti plasmid, Agrobacterium, tissue culture)

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: In the first commercial production of human insulin by recombinant DNA technology, the A and B polypeptide chains were made in separate E. coli cultures and then:

options.text: extracted and joined by creating disulphide bonds between them
joined end to end by peptide bonds formed by the enzyme DNA ligase
treated with enzymes to remove a C peptide from each chain
cut by restriction endonucleases and ligated into one plasmid

rows.explanation: Insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, A and B, held together by disulphide bridges. In the first recombinant production the chains were made separately in E. coli, extracted and joined by forming these bridges. DNA ligase joins nucleotides in DNA, not amino acids in a protein, and the C peptide belongs to proinsulin, not to separately made chains.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 Biotechnology and its Applications: genetically engineered insulin (chains A and B joined by disulphide bonds)

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following phases of a population growing in a limited habitat in the order in which they occur over time.
(A) Phase of deceleration
(B) Lag phase
(C) Asymptote near the carrying capacity
(D) Phase of acceleration
rows.explanation: Growth in a limited habitat is first slow (lag phase), then speeds up in the acceleration phase, slows again during deceleration as resources become limiting, and finally levels off at an asymptote near the carrying capacity. Putting acceleration before the lag phase ignores that the population needs time to adjust before it can grow rapidly.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 11 Organisms and Populations: population growth, logistic (sigmoid) growth phases

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Commensalism (B) Predation (C) Competition (D) Parasitism
List-II: (I) Cuscuta on a hedge plant (II) Orchid growing on a mango branch (III) Cactoblastis moth feeding on prickly pear (IV) Abingdon tortoise and introduced goats on Galapagos
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: An orchid growing on a mango branch benefits without harming the tree, which is commensalism; the Cactoblastis moth feeding on prickly pear is predation; goats and the Abingdon tortoise competed for the same food; Cuscuta draws nutrients from its host, which is parasitism. Exchanging the moth and the tortoise confuses a feeding relationship with competition for a shared resource.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 11 Organisms and Populations: population interactions with examples

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following events in the decomposition of dead plant litter in the correct order.
(A) Formation of dark, amorphous humus
(B) Release of inorganic nutrients from humus
(C) Breakdown of detritus into smaller particles by earthworms
(D) Degradation of detritus by bacterial and fungal enzymes
rows.explanation: Decomposition begins with fragmentation of detritus by detritivores such as earthworms, followed by catabolism by bacterial and fungal enzymes. Humification then forms dark humus, which is finally degraded by microbes in mineralisation, releasing inorganic nutrients. Enzymes act on detritus that has already been fragmented, so catabolism cannot come before fragmentation.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 12 Ecosystem: decomposition (fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification, mineralisation)

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Arrange the following in decreasing order of the amount of energy at each step of energy capture in a terrestrial ecosystem.
(A) Photosynthetically active radiation
(B) Gross primary productivity
(C) Net primary productivity
(D) Incident solar radiation
rows.explanation: Less than half of the incident solar radiation is photosynthetically active radiation, and plants capture only 2 to 10 per cent of that as gross primary productivity. Net primary productivity is what remains after the plants' own respiration is subtracted from GPP, so it is the smallest. Placing PAR above the incident radiation overlooks that PAR is only a fraction of total sunlight.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 12 Ecosystem: productivity, PAR, GPP and NPP

rows.subject: biology
rows.body:
Consider the following statements about ecological pyramids.
(A) The pyramid of biomass in the sea is generally inverted.
(B) A species that occupies two trophic levels is accounted for in an ecological pyramid.
(C) Ecological pyramids assume a simple food chain and do not accommodate a food web.
(D) Saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: The biomass of fishes can exceed that of phytoplankton, so the biomass pyramid of the sea is generally inverted, and pyramids assume a simple food chain and cannot represent a food web. Saprophytes are indeed given no place in them. Pyramids do not take into account one species belonging to two or more trophic levels, so the statement saying they do is false.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 12 Ecosystem: ecological pyramids and their limitations

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: Which of the following is NOT a reason suggested for the greater species diversity of the tropics compared with temperate regions?

options.text: Tropical latitudes have remained undisturbed for millions of years, giving species a long time to evolve
Tropical regions were repeatedly covered by glaciers, which forced their species to diversify rapidly
Tropical environments are less seasonal and more constant, which promotes niche specialisation
Greater solar energy in the tropics gives higher productivity, which supports more species

rows.explanation: The accepted explanations are a long, undisturbed evolutionary time, a less seasonal and more predictable environment that promotes niche specialisation, and more solar energy giving higher productivity. It was the temperate regions that suffered repeated glaciation, which eliminated species, so glaciation of the tropics is not a proposed reason.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 13 Biodiversity and Conservation: patterns of biodiversity, latitudinal gradient

rows.subject: biology
rows.body: Which of the following is an example of a broadly utilitarian argument for conserving biodiversity?

options.text: Forest plants yield timber, resin and medicines that can be sold
Every species has a right to exist whatever its use to humans
Pollinators in a forest raise the yield of crops on nearby farms
Wild relatives of crops are screened for new drugs and industrial products

rows.explanation: Broadly utilitarian arguments rest on ecosystem services such as pollination, oxygen release and aesthetic pleasure, so crop pollination by forest insects fits. Timber, resin, medicines and screening for new products are direct economic uses, which are narrowly utilitarian, and the right of a species to exist irrespective of its use is the ethical argument.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 13 Biodiversity and Conservation: why conserve biodiversity (narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian, ethical)

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body:
Arrange the following alkyl halides in decreasing order of their rate of reaction with aqueous KOH:
(A) 1-Chloropropane
(B) 1-Iodopropane
(C) 1-Fluoropropane
(D) 1-Bromopropane
rows.explanation: Breaking the C-X bond controls the rate, and the bond weakens down the group: C-F is strongest (about 452 kJ mol^-1 in CH3-F) and C-I weakest (about 234 kJ mol^-1 in CH3-I), while iodide is the best leaving group. For the same alkyl group the rate therefore follows R-I > R-Br > R-Cl > R-F. Ranking by bond polarity gives the reverse order, which is the common slip.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: nature of the C-X bond and reactivity of haloalkanes in nucleophilic substitution

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Bromoethane is heated with silver cyanide. The main organic product is:
rows.explanation: Silver cyanide is largely covalent, so the nitrogen end of the cyanide group attacks the carbon of the haloalkane and an isocyanide forms. Ionic KCN gives the alkyl cyanide (propanenitrile) instead. Nitroethane and ethyl nitrite come from the nitrite salts, AgNO2 and KNO2.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: ambident nucleophiles (CN- and NO2-) in nucleophilic substitution

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Phenol with bromine in carbon disulphide at low temperature (B) Phenol oxidised with chromic acid (C) Phenol treated with concentrated nitric acid (D) Phenol treated with dilute nitric acid at low temperature
List-II: (I) Benzoquinone (II) Mixture of o- and p-nitrophenols (III) 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (IV) Mixture of o- and p-bromophenols
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: In a non-polar solvent at low temperature phenol is brominated only mildly, giving o- and p-bromophenols, and chromic acid oxidises it to the conjugated diketone benzoquinone. Concentrated nitric acid nitrates all three activated positions to give picric acid, whereas dilute nitric acid at low temperature gives only the mono-nitro o- and p-isomers. Swapping the two nitration products is the usual slip.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: electrophilic substitution (halogenation, nitration) and oxidation of phenol

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Which reagent reduces ethanoic acid directly to ethanol?
rows.explanation: Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols by lithium aluminium hydride in dry ether, a very powerful hydride donor. Sodium borohydride is milder and reduces aldehydes and ketones but not carboxylic acids. Zinc amalgam with HCl converts C=O of aldehydes and ketones into CH2, and PCC is an oxidising agent.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers and Ch 8: reduction of carboxylic acids to primary alcohols with LiAlH4

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Drinking methanol can cause blindness and death because in the body it is oxidised to:
rows.explanation: In the liver methanol is oxidised first to methanal and then to methanoic acid. Methanal coagulates the protoplasm of cells and methanoic acid damages the optic nerve, which is why methanol is poisonous. Ethanal and ethanoic acid are the oxidation products of ethanol, and the mixed pairs result from carrying one alcohol's product into the other's second step.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: commercially important alcohols, methanol poisoning

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Sodium phenoxide is treated with bromomethane to give compound X. X is then treated with bromine in ethanoic acid in the absence of iron(III) bromide. The major product is:
rows.explanation: Sodium phenoxide and bromomethane react by Williamson synthesis to give anisole. The OCH3 group activates the ring and directs to the ortho and para positions, so bromination proceeds without a catalyst, and the less hindered para isomer is the major product. The ortho isomer is only the minor product, and meta substitution does not occur.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Williamson synthesis from phenoxide; halogenation of anisole

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Which one of the following is the correct name of CH3CH(Cl)CH2COOH in the IUPAC system?
rows.explanation: The longest chain containing the COOH group has four carbons, so the parent is butanoic acid, and the carboxyl carbon is always carbon 1. Counting on, CH2 is carbon 2 and the carbon bearing chlorine is carbon 3, giving 3-chlorobutanoic acid. Numbering from the methyl end, which puts chlorine on carbon 2, ignores that the principal functional group fixes carbon 1.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: IUPAC nomenclature of carboxylic acids

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Ethanal is treated with HCN, and the addition product is then hydrolysed with dilute acid. The final product is:
rows.explanation: HCN adds across the C=O group of ethanal to give the cyanohydrin CH3CH(OH)CN, and hydrolysis converts the CN group into COOH. The hydroxyl group stays on the same carbon, so the product is 2-hydroxypropanoic acid (lactic acid). Propanoic acid would require the OH to be lost, which does not happen, and no oxidation step is involved.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: nucleophilic addition of HCN, cyanohydrins

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Sodium propanoate is heated with soda lime. The organic product formed is:
rows.explanation: Heating the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with soda lime (NaOH and CaO) removes the carboxyl carbon as sodium carbonate: C2H5COONa + NaOH gives C2H6 + Na2CO3. The alkane has one carbon fewer than the acid, so ethane forms. Butane is the product of Kolbe electrolysis of the same salt, where two alkyl radicals couple.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: decarboxylation of carboxylic acids

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Propanoic acid is heated with methanol in the presence of a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid. The ester formed is:
rows.explanation: In esterification the acid supplies the acyl part and the alcohol supplies the alkyl part, with loss of water: CH3CH2COOH + CH3OH gives CH3CH2COOCH3 + H2O. The ester is named alkyl (from the alcohol) followed by alkanoate (from the acid), so it is methyl propanoate. Propyl methanoate results from swapping the roles of the acid and the alcohol.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: esterification of carboxylic acids with alcohols

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body:
Arrange the following in increasing order of acidic strength:
(A) Benzoic acid
(B) 4-Nitrobenzoic acid
(C) 4-Methoxybenzoic acid
(D) 4-Chlorobenzoic acid
rows.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups stabilise the benzoate ion and raise acidity, while electron-donating groups destabilise it. The nitro group withdraws strongly, chlorine withdraws by its inductive effect more than it donates by resonance, and the methoxy group donates by resonance, so it is the weakest acid, even weaker than benzoic acid. Placing methoxy above benzoic acid because of its electronegative oxygen ignores that resonance donation.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: effect of substituents on the acidity of benzoic acid

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Which one of the following does NOT give benzoic acid when heated with alkaline KMnO4 and then acidified?
rows.explanation: Vigorous oxidation of an alkylbenzene needs at least one hydrogen on the benzylic carbon, and then the whole side chain is oxidised to COOH whatever its length. The n-butyl, sec-butyl and isobutyl groups all have benzylic hydrogens and give benzoic acid. The tert-butyl group has none, so tert-butylbenzene is not oxidised.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: preparation of carboxylic acids by side-chain oxidation of alkylbenzenes

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Ethanal is treated with excess methanol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride gas. The final organic product is:
rows.explanation: Under dry HCl methanol adds to the C=O group of ethanal to give the hemiacetal 1-methoxyethan-1-ol. With excess methanol this reacts further with loss of water to give the acetal 1,1-dimethoxyethane. The hemiacetal is only the intermediate, and methyl ethanoate would need an oxidation step.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: nucleophilic addition of alcohols, hemiacetals and acetals

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: Ethanenitrile is treated with LiAlH4 in dry ether. The main organic product is:
rows.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces the C≡N group completely to CH2NH2, so CH3CN gives CH3CH2NH2 with the same number of carbon atoms. Methanamine would be the Hofmann bromamide product of ethanamide, which loses one carbon, and ethanal needs a partial reduction of the nitrile by SnCl2/HCl followed by hydrolysis.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 9 Amines: preparation of primary amines by reduction of nitriles

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body:
Arrange the following in increasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic bromination of the benzene ring:
(A) Aniline
(B) Benzene
(C) Acetanilide
(D) Nitrobenzene
rows.explanation: The lone pair of NH2 is donated strongly into the ring, so aniline is the most reactive. In acetanilide the nitrogen lone pair is also pulled towards the carbonyl group, so activation is weaker than in aniline but still greater than in benzene, while the NO2 group withdraws electrons and deactivates the ring. Placing acetanilide below benzene confuses weaker activation with deactivation.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 9 Amines: electrophilic substitution of aniline and the effect of acetylation on ring reactivity

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: What mass of sodium nitrite (molar mass 69 g mol−1) is needed to diazotise all the aniline used in the preparation?
rows.explanation: Each NH2 group consumes one molecule of nitrous acid, so 0.10 mol of aniline needs 0.10 mol of NaNO2, which is 0.10 × 69 = 6.9 g. Using two moles of nitrite per mole of aniline would give 13.8 g, but only one nitrous acid is used up; the extra hydrochloric acid, not nitrite, is what is taken in excess.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 9 Amines: diazotisation of aniline: stoichiometry of NaNO2 and HCl
rows.passage_text:
In a laboratory preparation, 9.3 g of aniline (0.10 mol) is dissolved in an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid, and the flask is kept in an ice-salt bath so that the temperature stays between 273 K and 278 K. A cold solution containing exactly the stoichiometric amount of sodium nitrite is added slowly with stirring. The clear solution obtained is never allowed to warm up and is used at once, without isolating any solid from it. It is then divided into four equal portions, labelled P, Q, R and S.

Portion P is poured into a cold alkaline solution of phenol, and an orange-red solid separates at once. Portion Q is treated with aqueous potassium iodide at room temperature; bubbles of a colourless gas escape and a dense, dark oil settles at the bottom. Portion R is added to a warm solution of cuprous cyanide and potassium cyanide; the same colourless gas is evolved, and a colourless liquid with a bitter-almond smell distils over. Portion S is simply left on the bench in a warm room for an hour; it also evolves the colourless gas, and its smell changes to that of a phenolic disinfectant.

Every reaction in this preparation goes to completion, and the organic products from P, Q and R all retain the benzene ring of the original aniline.

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body: The colourless liquid distilled from portion R is boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid until it is completely hydrolysed. The organic product is:
rows.explanation: Cuprous cyanide replaces the diazonium group by CN (Sandmeyer reaction), so portion R gives benzonitrile. Complete acid hydrolysis converts C≡N through the amide into COOH, giving benzoic acid with the same number of carbons. Benzamide is only the intermediate stage, and phenylacetic acid would need benzyl cyanide, which has an extra CH2.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 9 Amines: Sandmeyer reaction with CuCN and hydrolysis of the nitrile to the carboxylic acid

rows.subject: chemistry
rows.body:
Consider the following statements about the portions P, Q, R and S:
(A) Portion Q forms iodobenzene without needing a copper(I) catalyst.
(B) In portion P the diazonium ion attacks the phenoxide ring as a nucleophile.
(C) The phenolic smell of portion S arises because the diazonium ion is hydrolysed on warming.
(D) In portion R the diazonium group is replaced by CN with the help of a copper(I) salt.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
rows.explanation: Iodide replaces the diazonium group directly without copper, warm water hydrolyses the diazonium ion to phenol with loss of N2, and cuprous cyanide replaces the diazonium group by CN in a Sandmeyer reaction. In coupling the diazonium ion is the electrophile, not a nucleophile, so statement (B) is false; the phenoxide ring is the electron-rich partner.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 9 Amines: replacement and coupling reactions of benzenediazonium salts
